newsitem.title: SPAIN: Pro-ETA demonstration barred for fear of violence.
newsitem.headline: Pro-ETA demonstration barred for fear of violence.

text.p: The Basque regional government on Wednesday barred supporters of separatist guerrilla group ETA from going ahead with a weekend demonstration for fear it would turn violent.

Tensions have been running high in the Basque region of northern Spain since the rebels abducted young town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco last week and killed him after the government refused its demand for a prisoner transfer.

A government official in Madrid said the order to stop ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna from demonstrating on Saturday was given "to prevent incidents of violence". Herri Batasuna marches in the past have been flashpoints of violence.
The Basque Interior Ministry said in a statement: "Given the social tension over the murder of the councillor, it is likely there will be incidents during the demonstration."

Millions of Spaniards have vented their outrage at the rebels' latest killing in peaceful demonstrations, but there have been sporadic attacks on Herri Batasuna supporters and offices around the Basque region.
"It is a good decision by the Basque government and it has all the support of the Spanish government," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said of the order.
"This is a prudent act and shows that the thousands and thousands who demonstrated in the street did not do so in vain," he told reporters.

In response to Blanco's killing, the nationalist leaders of the Basque government have united with the central government in Madrid in a vow to isolate Herri Batasuna, a political party which holds seats in the Basque and Navarre regional parliaments and the national Congress.
Spanish politicians are mulling legal reforms that would restrict Herri Batasuna's activities, particularly demonstrations.
